target.name: Credit Limit
target.description: Assigns an unsecured credit limit to an applicant. A limit of $0 means the application was declined. Vendor documentation lists the accepted fields but discloses nothing about how they are weighed.

features.label: Debt-to-income
features.description: Monthly debt obligations divided by monthly income.

features.label: Credit history
features.description: Age of the oldest open tradeline in months.

features.label: Recent inquiries
features.description: Hard credit inquiries in the last 12 months.

features.label: Region
features.description: Region derived from the applicant's postal code.

features.label: Has mortgage
features.description: Whether the applicant holds an active mortgage.

experiments.title: Baseline response survey
experiments.design: Query each of 50 personas once to map the overall response surface.

experiments.title: Replicate probes · noise floor
experiments.design: Re-query 8 personas twice with identical inputs to measure response noise.

experiments.title: Validation set · progress monitoring
experiments.design: 32 uniformly random inputs used only to report progress during the run. Never used for training, query selection or stopping.

experiments.title: Sealed test set
experiments.design: 48 uniformly random inputs, never used for training or monitoring — scored once by the final surrogate.

experiments.title: Annual income · counterfactual pairs
experiments.design: Hold every other field fixed; set Annual income to $26.9k → $129k → $231k for each subject.

experiments.title: Debt-to-income · counterfactual pairs
experiments.design: Hold every other field fixed; set Debt-to-income to 3.2% → 40.0% → 76.8% for each subject.

experiments.title: Credit history · counterfactual pairs
experiments.design: Hold every other field fixed; set Credit history to 14 mo → 180 mo → 346 mo for each subject.

experiments.title: Recent inquiries · counterfactual pairs
experiments.design: Hold every other field fixed; set Recent inquiries to 0 → 5 → 10 for each subject.

experiments.title: Employment · counterfactual pairs
experiments.design: Hold every other field fixed; cycle Employment through salaried / self_employed / contract / unemployed for each subject (reference: salaried).

experiments.title: Region · counterfactual pairs
experiments.design: Hold every other field fixed; cycle Region through urban / suburban / rural for each subject (reference: urban).

experiments.title: Applicant age · counterfactual pairs
experiments.design: Hold every other field fixed; set Applicant age to 20 yr → 49 yr → 78 yr for each subject.

experiments.title: Applicant age · randomized null audit
experiments.design: Before accepting "no effect", 12 fresh subjects are queried at two random, stratified values of Applicant age each, looking for responses noise cannot explain.

result.summary: 0 of 12 pairs exceed the noise bound ±$2557 (max |Δ| $2000)

experiments.title: Has mortgage · counterfactual pairs
experiments.design: Hold every other field fixed; cycle Has mortgage through no / yes for each subject (reference: no).

experiments.title: Annual income · dose-response sweep
experiments.design: Sweep Annual income across 11 levels for 3 subjects, all other fields held fixed.

experiments.title: Debt-to-income · dose-response sweep
experiments.design: Sweep Debt-to-income across 11 levels for 3 subjects, all other fields held fixed.

experiments.title: Debt-to-income · threshold bisection
experiments.design: Bisect the interval 40.0%–48.0% on 2 subject(s) to localize the discontinuity.

experiments.title: Debt-to-income · confirmatory test
experiments.design: Fresh subjects queried at 41.4% vs 44.9% (either side of 43.1%) — a pre-registered test of the localized effect.

experiments.title: Credit history · dose-response sweep
experiments.design: Sweep Credit history across 11 levels for 3 subjects, all other fields held fixed.

experiments.title: Credit history · threshold bisection
experiments.design: Bisect the interval 0 mo–36 mo on 2 subject(s) to localize the discontinuity.

experiments.title: Credit history · confirmatory test
experiments.design: Fresh subjects queried at 23 mo vs 24 mo (either side of 24 mo) — a pre-registered test of the localized effect.

experiments.title: Recent inquiries · dose-response sweep
experiments.design: Sweep Recent inquiries across 11 levels for 3 subjects, all other fields held fixed.

experiments.title: Recent inquiries · threshold bisection
experiments.design: Bisect the interval 3–4 on 2 subject(s) to localize the discontinuity.

experiments.title: Recent inquiries · confirmatory test
experiments.design: Fresh subjects queried at 3 vs 4 (either side of 4) — a pre-registered test of the localized effect.

experiments.title: Annual income × Debt-to-income · 2×2 factorial
experiments.design: Annual income ∈ {$62.4k, $196k} × Debt-to-income ∈ {40.6%, 45.6%} on 8 subjects; difference-in-differences.

experiments.title: Annual income × Credit history · 2×2 factorial
experiments.design: Annual income ∈ {$62.4k, $196k} × Credit history ∈ {23 mo, 24 mo} on 8 subjects; difference-in-differences.

experiments.title: Annual income × Recent inquiries · 2×2 factorial
experiments.design: Annual income ∈ {$62.4k, $196k} × Recent inquiries ∈ {3, 4} on 8 subjects; difference-in-differences.

experiments.title: Annual income × Employment · 2×2 factorial
experiments.design: Annual income ∈ {$62.4k, $196k} × Employment ∈ {salaried, unemployed} on 8 subjects; difference-in-differences.

experiments.title: Debt-to-income × Credit history · 2×2 factorial
experiments.design: Debt-to-income ∈ {40.6%, 45.6%} × Credit history ∈ {23 mo, 24 mo} on 8 subjects; difference-in-differences.

report.summary: AUTOPSY evaluated 950 inputs on Credit Limit v3.2 (built-in synthetic target) across 36 experiments. 9 behavioral patterns are supported by controlled evidence (3 re-tested on fresh subjects), and 1 input field shows no detectable effect within the tested range and budget. 9 competing explanations were rejected. A 16-leaf surrogate tree reaches held-out predictive fit R² = 0.969 (MAE $1085) on 48 sealed test queries; this measures how well it predicts new responses, not the share of rules recovered.

rules.statement: Credit limit drops sharply once Debt-to-income exceeds 43.1%

rules.statement: Debt-to-income = 45.6% overrides Credit history: its effect vanishes (+$10.2k → ±$0.00)

rules.title: Applicant age is ignored
rules.statement: No detectable effect of Applicant age on credit limit within the tested range and budget

caveats: The target is stochastic (replicate SD ≈ $452); effects smaller than ±$1018 are treated as practically null.
Rules describe observed input→output behavior within the documented field ranges; behavior outside those ranges was not tested.
Statistical support is not proof of mechanism: a supported rule is the simplest explanation consistent with the controlled evidence collected, not a recovery of the target's source code.

22 hypothesis tests were run, each at α = 0.02 with no family-wise correction, so a small number of false positives is possible. 6 supported rules were not re-tested on fresh subjects; use "Test this finding" to check them.
"No detectable effect" means any effect was smaller than the noise-adjusted margin at this budget within the documented ranges, not that the effect is exactly zero.
Evidence scores are heuristics combining p-values, interval width and confirmation status. They are not calibrated probabilities that a rule is correct.
This is a built-in synthetic target built for demonstration; results on it are not real-world validation.
